title: Define target operators, namespace partitions, and the boundary between Bryan authority and user authority
desired_change: Declare supported operator roles and end-to-end jobs; add namespace/tenant/person partitions; distinguish founder canon authority from Bryan's personal preferences; require provenance, purpose, validity, and explicit promotion before personal context can become a system default.
expected_outcome: Quirk can support Bryan deeply without encoding Bryan as the universal tenant or requiring his intervention for every consequential decision.

risk.rights_or_safety_impact: Context bleed can create privacy, consent, identity, and authorization failures.

hidden_context_dependencies: The tribunal prompt requires target operators, but the PR names none.
The authority model is human-shaped but does not distinguish founder, operator, tenant owner, subject, reviewer, or end user.
Bryan's personal preferences and Quirk canon are not structurally separated.
No namespace or multi-tenant partition prevents preference or memory bleed.
No provenance class distinguishes native, reconstructed, and archaeological personal context.
acceptance_checks: At least three operator roles complete documented Golden Paths.
Personal PreferenceEdges cannot validate without purpose, context, authority, validity, and reference or explicit system default.
Cross-namespace access fails closed in tests.
Native, reconstructed, and archaeological context remain distinguishable.
